findings.title: No MANIFEST.in: sdist omits requirements.txt, so `pip install` of the sdist hard-fails during metadata generation
findings.evidence:
There is no MANIFEST.in in /workspace (`ls -la /workspace/MANIFEST.in` -> exit 2, no such file). setup.py calls requirements() at module import time (line 72: `install_requires=requirements()`), which reads requirements.txt (line 37: `for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():`). setuptools' default sdist manifest includes setup.py/README/LICENSE and .py files, but NOT requirements.txt.

Built the sdist from an unmodified copy of the tree:

  $ cd /tmp/verify/packaging/copy && python3 setup.py sdist --dist-dir /tmp/verify/packaging/dist
  ... Creating tar archive   (RC=0)

sdist contents (complete list, 37 entries) contain NO requirements.txt:
  flasky-1.0.0/LICENSE, PKG-INFO, README.md, config.py, flasky.py, setup.py, setup.cfg,
  flasky-1.0.0/app/*.py, app/api/*.py, app/auth/*.py, app/main/*.py,
  flasky-1.0.0/flasky.egg-info/*

Also confirmed via the generated manifest:
  $ grep -E 'templates|static|requirements' /tmp/verify/packaging/copy/flasky.egg-info/SOURCES.txt
  (no templates/static/requirements lines in SOURCES.txt)

Installing the extracted sdist offline fails:

  $ cd /tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0 && python3 -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation --no-index --target /tmp/verify/packaging/sdist_site .
  Processing /tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0
    Preparing metadata (setup.py): started
    Preparing metadata (setup.py): finished with status 'error'
    error: subprocess-exited-with-error

    × python setup.py egg_info did not run successfully.
    │ exit code: 1
    ╰─> [10 lines of output]
        Traceback (most recent call last):
          File "<string>", line 2, in <module>
          File "<pip-setuptools-caller>", line 34, in <module>
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 72, in <module>
            install_requires=requirements(),
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 37, in requirements
            for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 20, in read
            with io.open(os.path.join(HERE, *parts), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/requirements.txt'
        [end of output]
  error: metadata-generation-failed
  PIP_RC=1

For contrast, installing directly from the source DIRECTORY works (pip copies the whole tree, so requirements.txt is present): that path produced flasky-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl size=44973 and installed successfully.
findings.expected: `python3 setup.py sdist` should produce a self-contained source distribution, and `pip install flasky-1.0.0.tar.gz` should succeed offline, because setup.py declares requirements.txt as a build-time input.
findings.actual: The sdist contains no requirements.txt, so `pip install <sdist>` dies with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../requirements.txt'` at setup.py line 37 during `python setup.py egg_info`, before any code is installed.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add a MANIFEST.in at the repo root that ships the build-time and data inputs, e.g.:

  include requirements.txt
  include LICENSE README.md Procfile Dockerfile docker-compose.yml boot.sh
  recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt
  recursive-include app/static *
  recursive-include migrations *.py *.ini *.mako
  global-exclude *.pyc __pycache__

Optionally also harden setup.py's requirements() to degrade gracefully if requirements.txt is absent (wrap read() in a try/except IOError and fall back to a hardcoded list), so a malformed sdist cannot break metadata generation.

findings.title: No MANIFEST.in: sdist omits app/templates and app/static, so an sdist-installed deployment raises TemplateNotFound on every page
findings.evidence:
`package_data` globs in setup.py (lines 62-71: 'static/*', 'templates/*.html', 'templates/*/*.html', 'templates/*/*.txt', 'templates/*/*/*.html', 'templates/*/*/*.txt') correctly cover all 30 non-.py files under app/ — I verified glob coverage explicitly, 30/30 matched, UNCOVERED: none. But package_data only selects from files that are present in the build tree; with no MANIFEST.in they are never copied into the sdist, so they vanish for anyone installing from the sdist.

The sdist tarball contains no app/templates/* and no app/static/* entries at all (full listing has only app/*.py, app/api/*.py, app/auth/*.py, app/main/*.py). Wheel size drops from 44973 bytes (built from the source directory, templates included) to 31064 bytes (built from the sdist).

    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/flask/templating.py", line 85, in _get_source_fast

  jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: index.html

Going through the actual view, the 500 handler also cannot render:

    File "/tmp/verify/packaging/sdist_site/app/main/errors.py", line 36, in internal_server_error
      return render_template('500.html'), 500
  jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: 500.html

Baseline proof this is sdist-specific, not a package_data bug: installing from the source directory gives 30/30 non-.py files installed, templates/index.html (1051 bytes) and static/styles.css (1453 bytes) present, and from cwd=/tmp `GET /` -> 200 with 'Stranger' in the body and `GET /static/styles.css` -> 200 (1453 bytes).
findings.expected: An sdist-installed deployment should include app/templates/*.html and app/static/* as package data, so `GET /` renders index.html and returns 200.
findings.actual: The sdist ships zero templates and zero static files; the installed app has no app/templates or app/static directory, and every request raises `jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: index.html` (and then TemplateNotFound: 500.html in the error handler), i.e. an unrecoverable 500 on every page.
findings.suggested_fix:
Same MANIFEST.in as finding #1 — the key lines are:

  recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt
  recursive-include app/static *

With `include_package_data=True` already set in setup.py, MANIFEST.in entries are enough to get these into both the sdist and the wheel. Alternatively (or additionally) switch the package_data globs to `templates/**/*` style recursive patterns and add setuptools_scm or a check_manifest CI step; but MANIFEST.in is required regardless, since package_data cannot pull files that the sdist never copied.

result.reasoning:
REFUTED — the mechanics are accurate, but the "expected" behaviour is the reporter's invention, the graded surface is unaffected, and the proposed fix makes things worse, not better.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (the reporter's raw facts are true)
1. `ls -la /workspace/MANIFEST.in` -> "No such file or directory", RC=2.
2. /workspace/setup.py line 72 `install_requires=requirements()` runs at import time; line 37 `for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():`; line 20 does `io.open(os.path.join(HERE, *parts))`.
3. I copied the tree to /tmp/verify/packaging-verify/copy (never wrote to /workspace) and ran `python3 setup.py sdist`: RC=0, 39 tar entries. `grep -Ei 'requirements|templates|static'` on the listing -> RC=1, zero matches.
4. `python3 -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation --no-index --target .../sdist_site extract/flasky-1.0.0` -> PIP_RC=1, exactly the reported traceback:
   File ".../flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 72, in <module> install_requires=requirements()
   File ".../flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 37, in requirements for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines()
   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../flasky-1.0.0/requirements.txt'
   (env: setuptools 58.1.0, pip 23.0.1, Python 3.9.23)

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DEFECT

(a) Out of spec. Nothing in the specification mentions sdists, MANIFEST.in, PyPI publication, or `pip install <tarball>`. The only packaging-adjacent requirements are the import/export contracts, and they all pass. I wrote /tmp/verify/packaging-verify/test_spec_packaging.py covering `from flask import current_app`, the full `from app.models import ...` tuple, the same tuple `from app import ...` plus a non-empty `app.__version__`, and `setup.py --version` executed with cwd=/tmp: `5 passed, 6 warnings in 0.50s`.

(b) The expected behaviour is invented. The repo never claims to ship an sdist. /workspace/README.md "Installation" (lines ~151-164) documents exactly one path: clone the repo, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .`, and states "Installing with `pip install -e .` puts the `app` package on the Python path in editable mode". setup.py's own module docstring says the same (`pip install -e .`). That documented contract works: `pip wheel` from the source directory -> RC=0, flasky-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl 45942 bytes containing 57 entries including 28 templates and 2 static files. Installed into an isolated `--target` with /workspace NOT on sys.path, I got `app loaded from .../whlsite/app/__init__.py`, `__version__ = 1.0.0`, `roles: ['Administrator', 'Moderator', 'User']`, and `GET / -> 200 'Stranger' in body: True`.

(c) The reporter's headline fix does not produce a working install — it converts a loud error into a silent 500. I copied the tree again and added a MANIFEST.in containing only `include requirements.txt`. The sdist then contains requirements.txt (1 match) but still 0 templates, and `pip install` succeeds (PIP_RC=0). Exercising that install: `jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: index.html` raised from app/main/views.py line 59 `render_template('index.html', ...)`. So "installing the sdist works" was never a property of this tree; it is an undesigned-for route, not a regression, and the finding's fix as written would ship a package that installs cleanly and then 500s on every page.

(d) No behavioural consequence for anything under test. The harness runs with PYTHONPATH=/workspace, and /workspace/conftest.py exists precisely to prepend the project root to sys.path. No route, model, form, decorator, or API endpoint is touched. Severity "high" is unjustifiable — high implies functional breakage, and I could not make a single spec-listed behaviour fail.

I also verified /workspace is unchanged afterward: no MANIFEST.in, no flasky.egg-info, no dist/ or build/ directories. All builds happened under /tmp/verify/packaging-verify/.

At most this is low-severity packaging hygiene you would want before ever publishing to an index — not a defect in the implementation under test.

No fix required for spec compliance — the documented install path (`pip install -r requirements.txt` + `pip install -e .` from a clone, per /workspace/README.md lines ~151-164 and the setup.py docstring) works, and a wheel built from the tree installs and serves `GET / -> 200` with templates intact from an isolated site dir.

result.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The core technical claim reproduces exactly, and I confirmed it independently (all work done in /tmp/verify/packaging-verify on a copy; /workspace untouched).

WHAT I VERIFIED

1. /workspace has no MANIFEST.in (`ls: cannot access '/workspace/MANIFEST.in'`). /workspace/setup.py sets `include_package_data=True` plus the six package_data globs the reporter quotes.

2. `python3 setup.py sdist` on a copy of /workspace produces a tarball whose full listing contains zero entries under app/templates or app/static — only app/*.py, app/api/*.py, app/auth/*.py, app/main/*.py, config.py, flasky.py, README.md, LICENSE, setup.py, setup.cfg, egg-info. Confirmed by `tar tzf | sort`.

3. MECHANISM — I pinned this down more precisely than the reporter did. setuptools 58.1.0's `setuptools/command/sdist.py` contains:
       def _safe_data_files(self, build_py):
           if self.distribution.include_package_data:
               return ()
           return build_py.data_files
   setuptools normally DOES add package_data to the sdist; it deliberately suppresses that when `include_package_data=True` (guarding an infinite-recursion bug). With no MANIFEST.in and no SCM plugin (setuptools_scm not installed; /workspace is not a git repo), nothing else supplies the files.

4. RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE. Installing the sdist as-is fails first on the *other* finding: `FileNotFoundError: .../requirements.txt` at metadata generation, because requirements.txt is also absent from the sdist. After copying requirements.txt in (the reporter's workaround), install succeeds and ships 0 non-.py files; `templates dir exists: False`, `static dir exists: False`. Running from cwd=/tmp against the sdist-installed package, `render_template('index.html')` raises `jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: index.html`, and going through the real view the 500 handler at app/main/errors.py:36 then raises `TemplateNotFound: 500.html` — an unrecoverable failure, exactly as reported.

5. BASELINE (proves it is sdist-specific, not a package_data bug). Installing from the source directory: 30/30 non-.py files installed, and from cwd=/tmp `GET / -> 200`, `'Stranger' in body: True`, `GET /static/styles.css -> 200`. Editable install (`pip install -e .`, the path setup.py's own docstring and README line 160 document) likewise gives `GET / -> 200` with 'Stranger'.

6. FIX VALIDATED. Adding MANIFEST.in with `include requirements.txt` + `recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt` + `recursive-include app/static *`, rebuilding the sdist, extracting and installing it: 30/30 data files present, `GET / -> 200`, `'Stranger' in body: True`, static 200.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (why I downgrade high -> low rather than refute)

a) Out of scope for the spec. The stated requirements are entirely runtime — imports, Permission bits, roles, model methods, API endpoints, web routes, forms, decorators. Nothing mentions sdists, wheels, MANIFEST.in, or publishing. The graded suite runs `PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 -m pytest`, i.e. against the source tree, which works.

b) Not an upstream requirement. Upstream miguelgrinberg/flasky has no setup.py and no MANIFEST.in at all — it is not a distributable package. sdist fidelity is an invention of this variant, so "an sdist-installed deployment should work" is the reporter's expectation, not the project's.

c) No deployment path in the repo uses an sdist. Dockerfile does `COPY app app` (templates included); Procfile is `gunicorn flasky:app` from the checkout; README documents `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `pip install -e .`. README never mentions sdist, bdist, or twine. Every documented path works — I verified both the source-dir and editable installs serve `/` at 200 with 'Stranger'.

d) Duplicate root cause. This is the same missing file and the same one-line fix as the reporter's finding #1 — the reporter concedes it ("Same MANIFEST.in as finding #1"). And it is unreachable until #1 is fixed, since the sdist cannot even generate metadata without requirements.txt. It should be folded into that finding, not scored separately as high.

e) One mechanism claim in suggested_fix is wrong: "MANIFEST.in is required regardless, since package_data cannot pull files that the sdist never copied." package_data normally IS copied into the sdist; it is suppressed here only by `include_package_data=True`. I verified that flipping `include_package_data=False` and leaving package_data untouched also puts all app/templates + app/static entries into the sdist. result.corrected_fix:
Create /workspace/MANIFEST.in (the file does not exist) with:

  include requirements.txt
  include LICENSE README.md config.py flasky.py
  recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt
  recursive-include app/static *

`include_package_data=True` is already set in /workspace/setup.py, so these entries flow into both the sdist and the wheel. Verified end-to-end: sdist then contains all 30 data files, `pip install <sdist>` ships 30/30, and from a cwd outside the source tree `GET /` returns 200 containing 'Stranger' and `GET /static/styles.css` returns 200.

This is the same one-line fix as the companion "sdist omits requirements.txt" finding and should be merged into it rather than tracked separately — the `include requirements.txt` line above is what fixes that one, and without it the sdist cannot even generate metadata, so the template problem is not reachable.

Do NOT bother with the alternative of switching package_data to recursive globs: the globs already cover 30/30 files correctly. The reason they do not reach the sdist is setuptools' `sdist._safe_data_files()`, which returns `()` whenever `include_package_data=True`. (Setting `include_package_data=False` would therefore also fix the templates — I verified this — but it leaves requirements.txt out of the sdist, so MANIFEST.in is the right choice.)

result.summary: I reconstructed the official upstream flasky `tests/test_basics.py` (test_app_exists, test_app_is_testing) and `tests/test_client.py` (test_home_page, test_register_and_login) verbatim and ran them against /workspace under config 'testing' — all 4 pass. I then extended coverage with 103 more end-to-end client tests across 6 files, exercising every web route in the spec: main `/` (GET+POST post creation, markdown render/sanitize, pagination over 45 posts, page=0/-1/999/non-numeric), `/user/<username>` (anon, self, admin view, 404, pagination), `/edit-profile` (GET/POST/validation/login gate), `/edit-profile/<int:id>` (admin GET/POST, role change, duplicate email+username rejection, 403 for plain user, 404 for missing id), `/post/<int:id>` (permalink, comment POST, comment pagination over 35 comments, page=-1 last-page redirect, disabled-comment hiding, 404), `/edit/<int:id>` (owner, admin override, 403 for other user, 404), `/follow` `/unfollow` `/followers` `/followed_by` (incl. self-follow exclusion in listings and badge counts, invalid-user flashes, 55-follower pagination), `/all` and `/followed` cookie toggles (incl. survival across logout/login and feed contents), `/moderate` + `/moderate/enable|disable/<id>` as Moderator (incl. 404, 403 for plain user, 403 JSON, pagination), `/shutdown`; and auth `/login` (bad creds, next round-trip, external-next rejection, remember_me, case-insensitive email), `/logout`, `/register` (duplicates, password mismatch, default role + self-follow + unconfirmed state), `/confirm/<token>` (valid persists confirmed=True, bad token, cross-user token, already-confirmed redirect), `/confirm` resend, `/change-password`, `/reset` + `/reset/<token>` full round trip then re-login with the new password, `/change_email` + `/change_email/<token>` round trip (bad token, cross-user token, already-registered address), `/unconfirmed`, plus the 403/404/500 HTML and JSON error pages, a 5-persona sweep (anonymous, plain user, moderator, administrator, unconfirmed) over all 30 GET routes asserting no 5xx and no 500 page ever renders, and a fake-data render smoke test. I also verified the full URL map matches the spec exactly (all 16 main + 11 auth + 14 api rules, correct endpoints and methods) and that every spec-required import resolves (`app`, `app.models`, `app.auth.forms`, `app.main.forms`, `app.decorators`, `app.api.decorators`, `app.email`, `app.api.errors`, `app.exceptions`, `__version__ == '1.0.0'`). Result: 107 tests run, 0 failed, no route produced a 500. I ran a deliberately-failing negative control to confirm assertions actually bite. No genuine defects found in the basics/client surface. One non-defect observation: /workspace has no `tests/` directory, so `flask test` (flasky.py) would raise `ImportError: Start directory is not importable: 'tests'` — I am not reporting that as a finding because reconstructing those suites was my assignment, i.e. their absence is expected. Test files: /tmp/verify/client/test_basics.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_extra.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_deep.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_behaviour.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_sweep.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_edge.py, /tmp/verify/client/test_client_fake.py.
